name: NeurIPS 2024 LLM Privacy Challenge
description: A competition to identify privacy vulnerabilities in large language models (LLMs) and develop defenses to mitigate sensitive information leakage while maintaining model utility.

cr:input.name: Synthetic datasets
cr:input.description: Synthetic datasets inspired by real-world private datasets (e.g., Enron email dataset) with sensitive fields replaced by synthetic values. Includes text-based data with fields such as names, email addresses, and other sensitive data types. Example: 'John Doe' → 'Random Name'.
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: For the Red Team, the output includes extracted sensitive information (e.g., personally identifiable information) and the success rate of attacks. For the Blue Team, the output includes enhanced LLMs that prevent sensitive information leakage, along with metrics for defense effectiveness and model utility.

field.name: extracted_information
field.description: Sensitive information extracted by the Red Team. Example: 'Random Name'.

field.name: attack_success_rate
field.description: Success rate of Red Team attacks, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

field.name: defense_effectiveness
field.description: Effectiveness of Blue Team defenses in mitigating privacy risks, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

field.name: model_utility
field.description: General performance of the LLM after applying defenses, measured on standard tasks. Example: 0.85.

packages: [FILL IN THE BLANK: exact package versions for privacy toolkit and dependencies]

cr:evaluation.primaryMetric: [FILL IN THE BLANK: primary evaluation metric]
metrics: Efficiency (tokens/queries for Red Team, computational overhead for Blue Team)
cr:evaluation.notes: Attack Accuracy is higher for Red Team success but lower is better for Blue Team. Efficiency and Model Effectiveness are also considered, with statistical significance tests applied to results.
